subject: Social Science

sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: 125 8 – Unity in Diversity, or ‘Many in the One’ Unity in Diversity, or ‘Many in the One’ CHAPTER 8 Oh, grant me my prayer, that I may never lose the bliss of the touch of the one in the play of the many. — Rabindranath Tagore … The principle of unity in diversity which has always been normal to [India] and its fulfilment the fundamental course of her being and its very nature, the Many in the One, would place her on the sure foundation of her Swabhava and Swadharma. — Sri Aurobindo 1.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: What is meant by ‘unity in diversity’ in the Indian scenario?
sections.source_evidence: What is meant by ‘unity in diversity’ in the Indian scenario?

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: What aspects of India’s diversity are the most striking?
sections.source_evidence: What aspects of India’s diversity are the most striking?

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: How do we make out the unity underlying the diversity?

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: 126 Exploring Society: India and Beyond Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions A Rich Diversity If you travel through India by train, you will notice not only changing landscapes but also many different types of dresses and food; you will hear different languages, familiar and unfamiliar, and see different scripts on the way.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: Even within your own region, you will often come across people from other parts of India with different customs and traditions.
sections.source_evidence: Even within your own region, you will often come across people from other parts of India with different customs and traditions.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: This is India’s rich diversity, and it is usually the first thing that strikes visitors to our country.
sections.source_evidence: This is India’s rich diversity, and it is usually the first thing that strikes visitors to our country.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: With over 1.4 billion inhabitants (about 18 percent of the world’s population), such diversity is not surprising!
sections.source_evidence: With over 1.4 billion inhabitants (about 18 percent of the world’s population), such diversity is not surprising!

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: In the late 20th century, the Anthropological Survey of India, a national organisation, conducted a massive survey called ‘People of India project’ of 4,635 communities across all States of the country.
sections.source_evidence: In the late 20th century, the Anthropological Survey of India, a national organisation, conducted a massive survey called ‘People of India project’ of 4,635 communities across all States of the country.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: It counted 325 languages using 25 scripts; it also observed that many Indians may be called migrants, in the sense of people not living near their birthplace or with their original community.
sections.source_evidence: It counted 325 languages using 25 scripts; it also observed that many Indians may be called migrants, in the sense of people not living near their birthplace or with their original community.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: LET’S EXPLORE As a class activity, make lists of (1) the birthplaces of at least 5 classmates and the birthplaces of their parents; (2) the students’ mother tongues and other languages known to them.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: Discuss the results in terms of diversity.
sections.source_evidence: Discuss the results in terms of diversity.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: While diversity is indeed beautiful, making sense of it is not so easy.
sections.source_evidence: While diversity is indeed beautiful, making sense of it is not so easy.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Over a century ago, the British historian Vincent Smith wondered, “How, in the face of such bewildering diversity, can a history of India be written? … The answer to the query is found in the fact that India offers unity in diversity.” What is meant by ‘unity in diversity’?

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: How shall we perceive and express this unity, or the ‘Many in the One’?

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: To answer this question, we will explore a few dimensions of Indian life.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: Not to scale 127 8 – Unity in Diversity, or ‘Many in the One’ Food for All Some of you will have eaten food from different regions of India.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: The number of different dishes and preparations you can taste in India must be in their thousands, if not lakhs!

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: Yet certain food grains are common to almost every part of the country — cereals such as rice, barley and wheat; millets such as pearl millet (bajra), sorghum (jowar), finger millet (ragi); and pulses such as various kinds of dals and Fig.
